$comment: Approved differences from the Go output (PRD 20 Compatibility). Each golden entry names a case, a field (exit, stdout, stderr, tree, or file:<path>), and the exact allowed TypeScript value. The harness fails on any difference without an entry, on an entry whose exact value does not match, and on an entry that no longer matches a real difference. `actual` stays null while the case domain is pending; the port phase that enforces the domain sets it. `go_seed` lists P1 seed goldens (test/fixtures/go-seed/cli-goldens.json) that test/go-parity.test.ts expects to differ: each entry names the arguments and, in `allowed`, the exact TypeScript value of each field (exit, stdout, stderr) that may differ from Go. Every field not in `allowed` must equal Go, and every field in `allowed` must still differ from Go. Owner decisions: docs/work/2026-11-23-w1-r7-buildos-node-typescript-cli-rewrite/evidence.md#owner-decisions A platform exception class (`platform` and `cases`, for example PE-005) names cases whose Go output on that one operating system has a known defect: `go_observation_sha256` is the observationDigest (harness.ts) of the complete normalized defect observation (exit code, full normalized stdout and stderr, and the normalized filesystem snapshot of changes), taken from a real capture on that operating system and named in `go_observation_evidence`; `go_exit` and `go_text` (a text in `go_stream`) describe it for readers; capture.mjs on that operating system records such a case as `<id>-skipped` (for example `pe-005-skipped`) instead of writing or comparing it only when the digest matches exactly, and fails on any other output of a listed case; and `win32_golden` says which golden the platform uses: `shared` (the shared golden), or a source golden folder from which `capture.mjs --derive` makes a derived golden in os/<platform>/ (Windows path spelling, after each `windows_text` replacement, see CAPTURE.md). The harness accepts a derived golden only for a case listed here. `edge` lists entity edge goldens (test/fixtures/go-seed/entity-edge-goldens.json) that differ from Go: each entry names an edge case, a field (exit, stdout, stderr, or tree: JSON.stringify of the normalized file-tree snapshot, taken before the harness restores folder permissions, of the root and, as `../<name>`, the other files of the scratch folder, such as the manifest and an outside link target), and the exact allowed TypeScript value. test/entities-edge.test.ts (edgeExceptionProblems in harness.ts) fails on any other difference, on a value that is not the allowed one, on an entry whose field now equals Go, and on a case whose `exception` does not match its entries. `eval` lists conversion eval twins (test/conversion-eval/) whose body differs from the Go intake tool body for the same eval file (test/fixtures/go-seed/intake-eval-goldens.json, from scripts/capture-intake-eval-goldens.ts): each entry names the eval file, the twin part, the exact allowed TypeScript body (`actual`), and `added_blocks`, the Markdown blocks TypeScript adds; Go's body must equal `actual` with each added block and its following blank line removed once. test/intake-eval-parity.test.ts fails on any other eval difference, on a body that is not the allowed one, and on an entry that no longer differs from Go. PE-009 is a class exception: every PDF comparison with Go applies harness.ts pdfWordGapClass (the rule is stated in its `reason`). Its `pdf` entries are regression fixtures: each names a PDF body and the exact offsets of Go's body after normalizePdfWhitespace where the class check finds one added space (harness.ts pdfWordGapProblems); test/intake-eval-parity.test.ts and test/intake-hostile.test.ts check them. `intake_edge` (PE-010) lists intake write-target edge goldens (test/fixtures/go-seed/intake-edge-goldens.json, from scripts/capture-intake-edge-goldens.ts) that differ from Go, with the same fields and rules as `edge` over the whole scratch work folder ({ROOT}); test/intake-edge.test.ts checks them. `hostile` (PE-013 preflight cases and PE-015) lists cases of test/intake-hostile.test.ts that differ from Go: each names the case, Go's observed result for readers (`go`: exit, outcome, first stderr line; CI has no Go tool), and in `allowed` the exact TypeScript exit, stdout, and stderr ({PROJECT} stands for the project folder). That test fails on a case list that differs from its own and on any result that is not the allowed one. `p5_edge` lists P5 discovery and design edge goldens (test/fixtures/go-seed/p5-edge-goldens.json, from scripts/capture-p5-edge-goldens.ts) that test/p5-edge.test.ts expects to differ, with the same shape and rules as `edge`. `design_rollback` (PE-014) names test/design.test.ts promotion-rollback cases where Go's end state after an injected failure differs from the start state the port restores, with Go's end state for readers. `legacy_notice` (PE-016) maps each legacy invocation name to the exact stderr line it writes first; harness.ts stripLegacyNotice requires that line, removes it once, and compares the rest byte for byte.

exceptions.summary: A root that cannot be loaded gives exit 3 with the given root in Go filepath.Abs form and a typed diagnostic (root_unreadable, path_refused, or root_not_found), not an empty root and internal_error.
exceptions.reason: The exit code matches the seed and PRD 20. The envelope names the given root, and the typed diagnostic codes follow the TypeScript core error model. P3 set the exact values when it enforced the entities domain (P3 t8 and t11). The three cases are OS-dependent, so each entry names its operating system: the darwin and linux values are equal, and the win32 value spells the root with a backslash. A root with no `.os/data/` folder (a missing folder, a file, or a folder without `.os/data/`) gives `root_not_found` and `root <root> has no .os/data/ folder`. The result payload, mode, and write status equal the seed's. Scope extended by the owner on 2026-11-23 ("A, A, A", choice 1): a root folder that exists without `.os/data/` also gives exit 3, `root_not_found` with `root <root> has no .os/data/ folder`, and the given root; Go gives exit 3, an empty root, and `internal_error` (`resolve root "<root>": expected .os/data: stat <root>/.os/data: no such file or directory`). Only stdout differs. Edge golden `root-without-os-data`.

exceptions.summary: On Windows, the parity target of six apply and promote cases is the Go result on Linux and macOS, not Go 1.24.1's failed post-rename folder sync (`Access is denied.`).
exceptions.reason: Root cause: after Go renames the temporary file over the target, it opens the parent folder with os.Open and calls (*os.File).Sync() on it (the POSIX directory fsync pattern). On Windows, os.Open gives a read-only folder handle, Sync calls FlushFileBuffers, which needs write access, and Windows returns ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (`Access is denied.`). The rename has already committed, so Go reports a failure after the write landed: the entity cases exit 5 with write_status not_requested (and consolidate skips the index rebuild and its exit-6 recovery path), and the design cases exit 1 with a half-done promotion (the findings index row updated, no finding record or design file). Sync sites: toolkits/buildos/internal/entities/index.go writeIndexAtomic, toolkits/buildos/internal/entities/consolidate.go writeCanonicalAtomic, toolkits/buildos-design/internal/design/promotion.go syncDirectory. This contradicts PRD 20 (Windows support; exit 5 means a failure stopped a valid write from committing), PRD 17 Atomic Writes, and PRD 11 promotion. The TypeScript CLI must not reproduce the defect (P3 t14, P5 t11).
exceptions.rule: The win32 golden of each case is the Linux/macOS Go result, with Windows path spelling and Windows-only text where it legitimately differs. A shared case whose Go output on Linux and macOS prints no absolute path and no OS error text (`shared`) uses the shared golden on Windows. An OS-dependent case gets a derived golden in os/win32/, made by `capture.mjs --derive` from the committed linux golden (which must equal the darwin golden): in stdout and stderr (each JSON string decoded first), every `{ROOT}` followed by `/`-separated segments gets `\` separators, or `\\` when the `{ROOT}` directly follows a `"` (a Go %q string); each `windows_text` replacement is applied before that, on the raw stream (`scope` `raw`, first) or on each decoded JSON string (`json-string`), and must occur exactly once; `modes` is dropped (Windows has no permission bits); every other byte stays as captured. The result.json `derived` field names the exception, the source folder, and its SHA-256.
exceptions.owner_decision: docs/work/2026-11-23-w1-r7-buildos-node-typescript-cli-rewrite/evidence.md#owner-decisions (2026-11-23, PE-005 approved: option A, "on Windows, the parity target for the six cases where Go 1.24.1 fails its post-rename parent-directory sync (\"Access is denied\") is the Go behavior on Linux and macOS")

exceptions.summary: `entities consolidate` dry run writes nothing; the Go seed creates a temporary preflight folder in `.os/`.
exceptions.reason: The Go seed copies the eight datasets into `.os/.buildos-consolidation-preflight-<n>` and loads the copy, on a dry run too. The TypeScript CLI loads the same bytes from memory and writes nothing, as a dry run should (PRD 20: mutations are dry-run by default). Output is the same whenever Go's copy succeeds. They differ in two cases. 1: `.os/` is not writable. Go exits 5 with `create prospective graph directory: mkdir <root>/.os/.buildos-consolidation-preflight-<n>: permission denied` (ok false, internal_error); the TypeScript CLI exits 0 with the plan (ok true, no diagnostics). The file tree is the same (Go's mkdir fails). Edge golden `consolidate-dry-run-os-read-only`: exit and stdout differ. 2: the disk fills during the preflight copy. Go exits 5 with `write prospective input ...: no space left on device`; the TypeScript CLI exits 0. The review reproduced case 2; no golden covers it, because a full disk cannot be made portably in a test. No other difference is allowed.

exceptions.summary: A dataset symlink that points outside the root is refused (exit 3); the Go seed reads the outside file and replaces the link.
exceptions.reason: PRD 20 requires every read and write to stay inside the project root, and the filesystem port checks containment on the real path (`outside-root`). With `.os/data/personas.jsonl` a symlink to a file outside the root, `entities consolidate --apply` in the Go seed reads the outside file, writes the result into `.os/data/`, replaces the link with a regular file, and writes the index (exit 0, applied). The TypeScript CLI refuses (exit 3, ok false, `path_refused`, `.os/data/personas.jsonl resolves outside the root <root>`) and changes nothing: the link and the outside file stay. Edge golden `dataset-link-outside-root`: exit, stdout, and the file tree differ; stderr is equal. No other difference is allowed.

exceptions.summary: Text directly inside a div (an HTML callout) is kept as a paragraph; the Go converter drops it.
exceptions.reason: PRD 07 Contracts and Data requires that a converted document loses no section. Go 1.24.1 buildos-intake writes HTML text only from p, h1-h6, li, and table cells, so the text of a div box is lost (eval file html-visitor-policy: section "Callout note" lost, 93.37%). The TypeScript converter writes each run of text and inline elements directly inside a div as one paragraph, where it stands (src/core/intake/convert/html.ts). Sample Housing Cooperative

# Visitor and Guest Policy

This policy explains how members host visitors and overnight guests. It applies to all three buildings.

## Day Visitors

Members may host day visitors at any time. Visitors must leave the common room by 22:00 .

## Overnight Guests

A member may host an overnight guest for up to 14 nights in any 90-day period. Longer stays need written approval from the [membership committee](/committees/membership.html) .

- Tell the front desk the guest’s name and dates.

- Guests may not use the laundry room alone.

- Parking: guests use the visitor bays only. Bays V1 to V4 are in the north lot. Bay V5 is kept for deliveries.

### Approval Steps

- Fill in the guest form.

- Send it to the membership committee.

- Wait for the written reply, usually within five working days.

Note: Guests who stay longer than 30 nights in a year count as occupants under the lease.

## Shared Spaces

| Space | Guests allowed | Booking |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Common room | Up to 10 | Book at the front desk |
| Roof garden | Up to 6 | No booking |
| Guest suite | 2 per night | Book online, €25 per night |

Route for guests: front desk, then the common room, then the guest suite.

![Ground floor plan](media/visitor-policy-image-001.png)

[Mermaid diagram source](diagrams/visitor-policy-mermaid-001.mmd)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Member --> Form --> Committee --> Reply
```

## Questions

Ask at the front desk or email [desk@example.org](mailto:desk@example.org) .

Last updated 2 October 2026. Policy owner: membership committee.

exceptions.summary: Class exception: the port's PDF text may differ from Go's only by spaces between words that Go ran together.
exceptions.reason: Go github.com/ledongthuc/pdf GetPlainText joins every text run of one BT block with no separator, so a word gap drawn with a TJ offset, a Td move, or a line move inside one text object is lost (TwonewmembersjoinedtheboardinMarch.; MinutesMay meeting; QuarterlyStaff meeting). PE-009 is a class, not a list of cases. The rule, checked on every PDF comparison with Go (harness.ts pdfWordGapClass: the golden harness, the eval parity test, and the hostile-input tests): after normalizePdfWhitespace on both texts, the two texts must be identical after removing, from the port's text, only single spaces that sit at positions where Go has two adjacent non-space characters that the PDF renders as separate words. The PDF renders two characters as separate words when pdf.js puts a space between them inside one text run (a space character, or a TJ offset or glyph gap), or when they end and start two runs and the second run starts a new line (the baseline moves by more than half the larger font size), a new page, or more than 0.15 of its font size to the right of the end of the first (harness.ts pdfSeparations, computed from the PDF's runs, not from the port's output). No other character may differ, the port may never drop a space Go has, and the port's text must equal the PDF's runs with one space at each such run boundary, so it cannot add a space the PDF does not render. The check runs in both directions on every PDF twin (review round 3), also when the port text equals Go after white-space normalization: a port text that keeps Go's joined words (for example QuarterlyStaff meeting) fails, because it lacks a word gap the PDF renders. The `pdf` entries are regression fixtures, not the scope: for each, the class check must find exactly the recorded spaces. Without the gaps, eval file pdf-annual-report scores 97.67%, below the 98% gate. No golden case is affected: every PDF golden case equals Go after white-space normalization.

exceptions.reason: PRD 20 Output and Exit Contract: `--json` gives a stable automation form, and P5 A35 requires a dry run to report `planned` in JSON mode. The Go tools `buildos-discovery` and `buildos-design` define no `-json` flag: `--json` prints `flag provided but not defined: -json`, the flag usage, and exits 1. The TypeScript CLI (under `buildos discovery`, `buildos design`, and the legacy names) treats a whole `--json` argument in flag position as the switch: before the first non-flag argument, before `--`, and never as a flag value (Go `flag` rules). It prints the shared envelope (`discovery.run`, `discovery.qualify`, or `design.promote`; `write_status` `planned` for a dry run, `applied` for a write) on stdout with nothing on stderr, and the exit code of the human form. Every other spelling (`-json`, `--json=true`, `--title --json`, `-- --json`, `x --json`) behaves as in Go (P5 edge goldens `design-json-*`, `discovery-json-*`). P5 edge goldens `design-json-in-flag-position` and `discovery-json-in-flag-position`: exit, stdout, and stderr differ; the tree is equal (a dry run). No other difference is allowed.

A symlink at the discovery index (`runs.jsonl` or `findings.jsonl`) is PE-014. The option applies to write destinations only: content reads stay inside the root in every mode.

exceptions.summary: A failed convert leaves no files behind: side artifacts are written only after the whole source has been read and checked; Go writes each one as it meets it.
exceptions.reason: Input files are untrusted. Go writes xl/media and word/media files (and HTML images, SVG, and Mermaid files) while it reads the source, so a source that then fails leaves files behind. The port reads and checks the whole source first (every input limit, every XML part, every relationship), then writes the same side artifacts in the same order with the same --force checks, then the twins. A valid source gives the same output as Go. Only intake-convert-xlsx-escaping-target changes: Go writes system/assets/escaping-sheet/media/image1.png and then fails on the escaping relationship; the port fails with the same message and writes nothing. No other difference is allowed. Preflight cases (W1 R7 P4 review round 3, `hostile`): an HTML page with one image, whose side artifact system/assets/page/media/page-image-001.png Go writes before the twin system/assets/page/page.md, and a condition at the twin that exists before the convert: a folder at the twin with --force, an existing twin without --force, a read-only twin with --force, and a read-only twin folder (with media/ already there) with --force. Go writes the side artifact and then fails; the port checks every write first, in Go's order (folder creation, existence against --force, the entry's type, the open of an existing entry, a new entry's folder, link count, containment), fails with the same exit code and text, and writes nothing. In a hostile entry, {PROJECT} stands for the project folder. The go fields come from a Go 1.24.1 buildos-intake run on macOS on 2026-11-23; test/intake-hostile.test.ts checks that its PE-013 preflight cases are exactly these and that each port result equals the pinned one.

exceptions.summary: A failed promotion is fully undone: the port restores the start state after any promotion failure, where Go can leave changed bytes or a changed link type; a symlink at the discovery index (`runs.jsonl` or `findings.jsonl`) is replaced, never followed, where Go appends through it.
exceptions.reason: PRD 20 requires a failed write to leave the project as it was. Promotion rollback: before the first write, `design promote finding` records each entry it replaces (the bytes and full mode of a file, with its setuid, setgid, and sticky bits, which Go's rollback drops, or the text and own mode of a symlink), and after any failure it restores that start state, removes the design file it created, and leaves no temporary file. The error text and exit code are Go's. The Go 1.24.1 design tool, with the same injected failures (a scratch Go test in package design that wraps replaceExistingFile and createExclusiveFile, on test/fixtures/golden/design), ends in another state in five of six cases, listed in `design_rollback` with Go's end state; the sixth (the design creation fails on regular files) ends in the start state in Go too and is not an exception. test/design.test.ts "a failed promotion restores every replaced entry as it was" checks the start state in all six cases and that this list names exactly the five cases where Go differs. Discovery index: discovery adds its index row with an atomic replace (the index as it is plus the new line, renamed over the entry), not Go's append, so a failed write leaves the old index; a symlink at the index, to a file outside or inside the root, is replaced by a regular file with exactly the bytes Go writes through the link, and the link target is kept, also with `--allow-outside-root`. P5 edge goldens `discovery-runs-index-link-outside`, `discovery-runs-index-link-outside-allowed`, and `discovery-runs-index-link-inside`: only the tree differs, by exactly the values below. A consequence of the same index-replacement rule (orchestrator ruling, 2026-11-23; the owner is informed): with a writable (0644) runs.jsonl in a folder the user cannot write (0555), Go opens the index in place, appends, and exits 0; the atomic replace must create a temporary file in that folder, so the port exits 1 with `open <index>: permission denied`, keeps the old index bytes, and removes the run folder it created. P5 edge golden `discovery-runs-index-folder-readonly`: exit, stdout, stderr, and tree differ, by exactly the values below. No other difference is allowed.

exceptions.summary: Make Docs 2.0.9 design inputs, the installed-root rule, and read bounds. The owner approved each of these differences from the Go tools: (1) buildos design promote with a Make Docs design input that is missing or empty, in a project with no legacy docs/assets/ layout, stops with exit 3 and a plain message (Go: exit 1, read design router ...: open ...); (2) a project with a complete Make Docs 2.0.9 layout (.make-docs/system/ bodies and docs/designs/AGENTS.md, no docs/assets/) promotes a finding (Go fails there with exit 1); (3) a mixed project, with a valid .make-docs/system/ body for an input and an empty or absent legacy docs/assets/ body, promotes a finding (Go fails on the legacy body); (4) every Make Docs design input, legacy ones too, is read inside the project only: a link to a regular file inside the root is read, a link that leads out of the root stops with exit 3 (outside-root), and a body larger than 4 MiB is not read (Go read any file through any link); (5) a root with a .os/ folder but not all of .os/, assets/, docs/, playbooks/, and workspace/ (a project made by buildos init --skip-make-docs has no docs/) is an installed project in every domain, unless system/.os/ is a folder too and .os/manifest.json is not a file (Go read such a root as a source checkout and failed with exit 1 at its first system/... read); (6) every file read has a size bound (128 MiB for data and indexes, 64 MiB for discovery and design documents, 4 MiB for Make Docs inputs, 512 MiB for intake files): a larger file fails with exit 1 or the domain's own read diagnostic and the text read <path>: file too large: BuildOS reads at most <bound> from one such file (Go read any size). Output equals Go byte for byte only for a project that uses the legacy docs/assets/ inputs with no link at them, with all five Go folders or a source layout, and files within the bounds: every design, discovery, intake, and entities golden is such a case.

The orchestrator directed: a valid local .make-docs/system/ body first, then the legacy location with Go's error text, else a clear stop (PRD 20 exit code 3: a required input cannot be loaded). Review round 2: the stop distinguishes three cases from the same rules buildos init uses (P7-R2-03); Make Docs inputs are read inside the root and bounded (P7-R2-02; PE-012 approves contained content reads for writes' domains, but not the in-root link rule or the bound); PRD 05 Installed Project Paths makes docs/ optional, so the five-folder Go rule misread a supported project (P7-R2-01); every read is bounded (P7-R2-02, SECURITY.md Read Safety). No golden case covers these inputs, so the goldens stay unchanged. test/design.test.ts, test/installed-layout.test.ts, and test/fs-port.test.ts pin the exact results.

exceptions.summary: HTML images: intake convert reads a local image an HTML document names only when its real path is inside the folder that holds the HTML file (for an HTML folder source, the selected folder) or inside the project root. Any other image is not read and not copied; the twin keeps Go's [Uncopied image: <alt>](<src>) link, stderr gets one line buildos-intake: warning: did not copy image <src> from <document>: <reason>, and the command exits 0. An image over 512 MiB gets the same treatment with the bound as the reason. W1 R7 P7 review round 4 (P7-R4-03): the image address is percent-decoded once before that check (my%20image.png names my image.png), so an encoded ../ is refused like a plain one; when no file has the decoded name, the address as written is tried, as Go read it; an address with an invalid escape is used as written; an address that decodes to a zero byte is not read (a warning, exit 0). The warning ends: The converted file has an "Uncopied image" marker with the address as the document gives it; that address is relative to the document, not to the converted file. Go read any path (absolute, ../ out of every folder, or through a link) and copied its bytes into the project, and did not decode an address, so an in-tree image whose address held a percent escape was left uncopied.

exceptions.summary: Explicit paths and read-back sizes: (1) a relative path the user names (intake --source, a non-default --assets-root, --output, or --playbooks-root; discovery --evidence, --raw-finding, --confirmation-test, --confirmation-evidence) is used as written in an installed project that has an entry named system at its root; Go dropped the leading system/ there too, so system/inputs/report.csv read inputs/report.csv. In an installed project with no system entry, the legacy system/ spelling is still dropped, as in Go; BuildOS-owned defaults (--assets-root system/assets and the default index paths) keep Go's translation in every installed project. (2) A write of a file BuildOS reads back (the discovery runs and findings indexes and run and finding records, the findings index and finding record of a promotion, the intake playbooks and references indexes and converted twins, the canonical datasets and the entity-resolution index of entities) that would be larger than that file's read bound stops before any write with exit 4 (file_too_large_to_read_back), the dry run too; and (review round 4, P7-R4-02) a JSONL row that its reader could not read stops the same way (exit 4, row_too_long_to_read_back): a new or rewritten row of .os/data/runs.jsonl or .os/data/findings.jsonl of 64 KiB or more (discovery run, discovery qualify, design promote, entities consolidate; discovery and design read these files line by line with Go's 64 KiB bufio.Scanner token), and a rewritten row of any other governed dataset of 16 MiB or more (entities consolidate; the entity graph's line limit). Go wrote it, and the next command failed (exit 1, bufio.Scanner: token too long). (3) Final check (P7-F-04): when discovery run or discovery qualify adds a row to .os/data/runs.jsonl or .os/data/findings.jsonl and the file does not end in a line feed, a line feed goes before the new row; Go appended the row directly (os.O_APPEND, toolkits/buildos-discovery/internal/discovery/discovery.go appendJSONL), so the new row joined the last row on one line and the next command failed (exit 1); with a valid 65,000-byte last row Go wrote one 66,392-byte line. The read-back checks of (2) run on the exact bytes of the append, separator included, before dry-run success or any write.
exceptions.reason: W1 R7 P7 review round 3 (P7-R3-01, P7-R3-04). (1) Go's resolvePath and resolveRepoPath (toolkits/buildos-intake/internal/intake/convert.go, toolkits/buildos-discovery/internal/discovery/discovery.go) apply installedRootRel to every relative path in a five-folder project, explicit ones included, so a user-owned system/ folder was silently remapped; the port's installed-root rule (PE-017 behavior 5) made this reach a project from buildos init --skip-make-docs too. No golden case names a system/ path in an installed project, so every golden is unchanged. (2) PE-017 behavior 6 bounds every read; without a write check, a run index at exactly 128 MiB took one more row and the next command failed (exit 1). test/review-round-3.test.ts pins both. Review round 4 (P7-R4-02): a readable 65,534-byte findings row passed a promotion dry run, promotion grew it to 65,561 bytes, and the next promotion exited 1; every JSONL writer now checks each row it writes against its reader's line limit. test/review-round-4.test.ts pins it.

exceptions.summary: Make Docs 2.0.9 design text: in a project whose design template resolves from the Make Docs 2.0.9 layout (.make-docs/system/templates/design.md), buildos design promote finding writes the design in the 2.0.9 form, built from that template and checked against the project's design contract; a project whose template resolves from the legacy docs/assets/ layout keeps the Go bytes exactly.
exceptions.reason: W1 R7 P7 Stage 6 (t20, t21; register R-009, owner option B). The Go text has no frontmatter, no ## Human Experience Intent section, a Next Prompt link ../assets/prompts/<prompt> that does not resolve in a 2.0.9 project, and the source path system/docs/designs/ in its text, so every design promoted in a standard 2.0.9 project broke the Make Docs 2.0.9 design contract. Scope, exactly: (1) the form follows the design template promotion read: a template from .make-docs/system/ (the 2.0.9 layout) gives the 2.0.9 form, a template from docs/assets/templates/ gives Go's bytes; (2) the 2.0.9 form is the template's frontmatter with title, route, prompt file, why, and coordinate handoff filled and its comment lines left out, then # <title>, then every ## section of the template in the template's order: Purpose, Context, Decision, Alternatives Considered, Consequences, and Intended Follow-On carry the Go text (the router named as docs/designs/), every other section (Human Experience Intent, Performance Evidence Candidates) is the template's own text, unfilled, for the planner; (3) the Next Prompt line is the template's line with a relative link to the prompt file promotion read (so it resolves) and the make-docs://system/prompt/<prompt> URI; (4) a template or contract of a form this version does not know stops the promotion with exit 3 (make_docs_design_form_unknown) before any write. The findings index and the finding record are byte for byte the same as in Go's form; PE-014 rollback holds. No golden case has a 2.0.9 template, so every golden is unchanged; test/design.test.ts (Stage 6) pins the form, the link and URI resolution against the committed 2.0.9 companion fixture, the fail-safe cases, and the rollback. Review round 4 (P7-R4-04, P7-R4-05), inside the same form: the template's frontmatter must be the 2.0.9 lines exactly (each filled value double-quoted) and the contract's required headings the 2.0.9 list in its order, held by the template in that order, or the promotion stops with exit 3 before any write; placeholders are checked on the template before any value is put in, and values are put in once; the frontmatter title is a YAML double-quoted scalar with every non-printable character escaped; the # title line is one line (line breaks as spaces, a leading # escaped); in each section BuildOS fills, a line start that Markdown reads as a heading, setext underline, code fence, or HTML block is escaped with a backslash (final check, P7-F-06: a balanced fenced code block in finding text is kept byte for byte, and only a fence with no closing fence is escaped); final check, P7-F-05: every template placeholder must be a 2.0.9 placeholder in its 2.0.9 section and the Next Prompt line must be the 2.0.9 line exactly, or the promotion stops with exit 3 before any write, and the rendered Next Prompt line is checked to be the relative link; the result is read back (the YAML subset reader, a strict double-quoted reader, and the heading list) and a failure writes nothing (exit 3, design_self_check_failed). A design for an ordinary title and finding is unchanged.
